Building libmackie

A hand-kept Makefile, no build system to configure. You need a C11 compiler and make. Nothing else: no library outside libc, not even libm.

make                          # libmackie.a
make shared                   # libmackie.so.<version>, with its soname links
make test                     # the unit suite, the same command CI runs
make install PREFIX=/usr/local [DESTDIR=...]
make clean

The code is plain C11 built with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, so a warning is a build failure. CC and CFLAGS can be overridden on the command line; the warning flags are kept even then.

make install copies the headers to $(PREFIX)/include/mackie/, the archive to $(PREFIX)/lib (LIBDIR= to change it) and a pkg-config file, so a consumer builds with:

cc app.c $(pkg-config --cflags --libs libmackie)

Tests

Every test runs through tests/run-test.sh, which gives it a timeout: a hang is a failure, never a stalled build. A test that exits 77 proved this machine cannot host it and is reported as SKIP, never as a pass.

  • test_mcu is the TypeScript MCU suite ported case for case: faders, buttons, V-Pots, meters, scribble strips, the handshake ground truth and the scribble backlights, with the refusals a C API adds.
  • test_golden holds every encoder and decoder to tests/golden/mcu_golden.h, the bytes the TypeScript encoders sent and what the TypeScript decoders read for the same inputs, and checks that what the encoders send decodes back to what they were given.
  • test_install.sh installs into a scratch root and builds a consumer through pkg-config; conformance-packaging.sh holds the version and soname copies to one another; test_workflows.sh parses the CI workflows; public-sources-check.sh and its own test keep private names out of the tree and the history.

The golden bytes

tests/golden/mcu_golden.h is generated, and committed. To compare against a TypeScript MCU module (compiled to mcu.js, with its dependencies resolvable from where it sits):

node tools/gen-goldens.mjs path/to/mcu.js > tests/golden/mcu_golden.h
git diff tests/golden/mcu_golden.h

A difference in the header is a change of wire bytes on one side or the other. The generator draws its sampled inputs from a fixed seed, so the same module writes the same file.
